**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — INDEMN.**

- **What the document does:** Article XII (p0128–p0129) contains only a Licensee→Licensor indemnity, and a very broad one (exercise of the licence, conduct of Licensee's business, any breach). No Licensor indemnity exists anywhere. Article XIII(a) then expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology, and the warranty disclaimer excludes non-infringement.
- **Why it fails:** This is walk-away territory under the rule — no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity covering the Vendor's own technology.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted a Licensor defence/indemnity for (a) IP infringement allegations, (b) breach of law, (c) Licensor-caused data incidents, (d) gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a "notwithstanding Article XIII" opener so the liability exclusion does not gut it; and narrowed the Licensee indemnity to Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of law. Fallback (customary exclusions plus a 3× annual fee super-cap) offered in the comment.
